source.title: String .extractUrl() includes trailing sentence punctuation in the extracted URL

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

`.extractUrl()` includes punctuation that belongs to the surrounding sentence, not the URL itself. When a URL appears at the end of a sentence, before a comma, or inside parentheses, the extracted value keeps the trailing marks:

- `"Docs: https://docs.n8n.io.".extractUrl()` → `https://docs.n8n.io.` (trailing period included)
- `"See (https://example.com) for details".extractUrl()` → `https://example.com)` (closing paren included)
- `"Visit https://example.com, then come back".extractUrl()` → `https://example.com,` (comma included)
- `"File at https://example.com/data.csv;".extractUrl()` → `https://example.com/data.csv;`

The returned value is then not directly usable: passing it on (e.g. to `new URL()`, an HTTP request, or `.extractUrlPath()`) fails or hits the wrong path.

The same code exists in `packages/workflow/src/extensions/string-extensions.ts` and its mirror in `@n8n/expression-runtime`.

### To Reproduce

1. In any expression, evaluate: `{{ "Docs: https://docs.n8n.io.".extractUrl() }}`
2. The result is `https://docs.n8n.io.` — the sentence-final period is part of the URL.

The regex match in `extractUrl` (`URL_REGEXP`) ends with `#?[^\s]*`, which consumes every non-whitespace character after the host, including sentence punctuation.

### Expected behavior

Punctuation directly after a URL that belongs to the surrounding sentence is not part of the extracted URL:

- `"Docs: https://docs.n8n.io.".extractUrl()` → `https://docs.n8n.io`
- `"See (https://example.com) for details".extractUrl()` → `https://example.com`
- Balanced parens that are part of the URL are kept: `"Wiki (https://example.com/C_(lang))"` → `https://example.com/C_(lang)`
- Query strings are unaffected apart from a trailing sentence mark: `"Search https://example.com/search?q=n8n!".extractUrl()` → `https://example.com/search?q=n8n`

This matches how other ecosystems handle URLs in prose (e.g. CommonMark/GFM autolinks trim trailing punctuation and unbalanced closing parens).

### Debug Info

Found by reading the code on `master` (2.45.0). The regex has behaved this way since the current matching was introduced in #6010.

### Operating System

Platform independent

### n8n Version

master (current HEAD)

### Node.js Version

24

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: I checked the current source: both `packages/workflow/src/extensions/string-extensions.ts` and `packages/@n8n/expression-runtime/src/extensions/string-extensions.ts` use the same `URL_REGEXP`, and `extractUrl()` returns `matched[0]` unchanged. So a trim added to only one implementation would leave the expression-runtime behavior inconsistent. For the examples here, trimming terminal prose punctuation should also preserve balanced parentheses that are part of the URL (and only remove unmatched closing `)`), rather than stripping punctuation indiscriminately.
